parts.label: Part 3
parts.article:
Becky, hi. What are you doing here at the college?

Hi, Jason. Just using the library. What about you?
I'm taking the PSW programme. You know, personal support worker.
No kidding. I've just qualified as a PSW.
Really? I'd love to talk to you about the programme.
Okay. Well, first off, the main duties they taught me here were exactly what I needed on the job.
You mean like bathing and dressing people?
Yes, young and old need this. You'll work with people of all ages, from young people with disabilities to seniors. But you know, nothing really prepares you for how alone many people are. They crave conversation. And I don't mind chatting with them while I work, though that's not officially in my job description.
I think I'd like to focus on seniors' care. And with the country's older population growing, maybe I'll get a job fast. Do we have to be responsible for any medications?
No, that's not for us to do. And while you will prepare meals, you won't feed people. But working to keep clients healthy and able to live on their own without risk as long as possible is always the goal. And we're recognising that, with life spans increasing, long-term care facilities won't be able to keep up with the demand, and carers who will need care.
I almost didn't meet the requirements for entry into the PSW programme. I was one course short of getting my high school diploma, so I had to go back to summer school. I took science because I'm no good at maths. Oh, and speaking of not getting in, having my first aid certificate was a real piece of luck. I would have been turned down without that too.
And I would have had a problem with immunisations, except that I travelled the year before. And when the doctor checked my records, they were up to date. I also had to hand in a written essay on why I wanted to be a PSW.
So, Becky, what did you think about the courses you had to take in the personal support worker programme?
Well, I used to think I got my points across pretty well with people until the Understanding Is Essential course. For starters, it taught me how to express myself much more effectively. I also learned a lot about preparing clear reports for my supervisors and dealing in a better way with people in general — you know, giving facts without personal views. You'll find that you need those skills every single day.
I'm enjoying the Foundations course. I'm taking it now, and I'm getting a lot out of it because support workers are a newer level of care in the province. I think we absolutely have to understand how we fit into the overall system. It's a great place to voice your opinions freely. Some are quite personal. Did you have to take a course called The Way We Work? I didn't know psychology was part of the programme.
That course was a favourite of mine, but it's probably not what you're thinking, Jason. It's about what happens on the inside of the body and covers the functions that keep our bodies operating well. Even if you're not a PSW, the course is really interesting. I learned so much.
What do you think about Residence Care? I know the thinking now is that long-term care facilities aren't the answer for our ageing population.
Right. And so this course zeros in on the changes people can make to their homes so they can stay there, like installing higher toilets, for example. You'll also learn about specialised equipment people can get to help themselves — safety bars for the shower and so on.
Do any of the courses focus on the families of our clients? After all, any kind of illness or disability affects everybody.
So true. And yes, there is one. It's called Dynamics. You usually get it in your last term. You'll learn different strategies to help relieve some of the anxiety and strain that happens within the family. I got a lot out of that course. It's the only one that focuses on emotions rather than facts. I think giving people this kind of help is just as important as any kind of expensive equipment they buy to help themselves.
The course I'm really looking forward to is The Power Within.
Oh, it's terrific. Getting old has quite an impact on the mind, as you know. But you'll be taught ways to help clients keep the mind active so they're not so forgetful. You'd be surprised how much improvement you can see in clients when you apply these methods.

analyses.content: 录音中男生确认了“洗澡和穿衣（bathing and dressing）”是需要的，这属于生理需求（physical needs），对应选项 C。
"You mean like bathing and dressing people? Yes, young and old need this."
注意区分，不要因为后面提到“做饭”就选 B，录音特意强调了“不喂饭”。

analyses.content: "I was one course short of getting my High School diploma, so I had to go back to summer school."
听到 "maths"（数学）不要选 B，数学只是他挂科的那一门课，真正的门槛是整个高中毕业证。
男生提到他因为缺一门课没拿到高中毕业证，必须去读暑期学校补上才能入学，说明高中学历（High school diploma）是硬性要求。

analyses.content: "Oh, and ... having my first aid certificate was a real piece of luck. I would have been turned down without that too."
听到 "essay" 别选 C（语言资格），essay 只是申请材料之一，并非资格证；听到 "immunizations"（免疫证明）也不用选，因为选项里没有。
男生明确说，如果没有急救证书（first aid certificate），他也会被“拒之门外（turned down）”，证明这是必备条件。

analyses.content: "...taught me how to express myself much more effectively... I also learned a lot about presenting clear reports to my supervisors..."
不要只看课程名字瞎猜，要听课程内容的实际描述（表达、汇报）。
录音提到学会了“有效表达自己（express myself）”和“做清晰的汇报（presenting clear reports）”，对应职场沟通（Workplace communication）。
录音强调要理解我们如何“融入整个系统（fit into the overall system）”，对应 PSW 在医疗体系中的角色。
"...we absolutely have to understand how we fit into the overall system."
"System" 这个词很大，在这里指代的就是整个 Health Care 体系。
"...covers the functions that keep our bodies operating well. Even if you're not a PSW, the course is really interesting."
录音先提到了 "psychology"（心理学），但紧接着男生纠正说主要是关于 body operating 的，所以排除心理相关选项。
录音解释说课程涵盖了“维持身体运作的功能（functions that keep our bodies operating）”，对应生物学方面（Biological aspects）。
"...changes people can make to their homes so they can stay there. Like installing higher toilets... special equipment people can get to help themselves..."
听到 "toilets" 或 "equipment" 不要困惑，这些都是为了支持独立生活而举的例子。
录音提到改造家庭环境让人们能“待在家里（stay there）”并“自助（help themselves）”，对应独立生活（Independent living）。
"You'll learn different strategies to help relieve some of the anxiety and strain that happens within the family."
这里的 "family" 指的是客户的家庭，重点在于解决由此产生的压力，而不是家庭本身。
关键词是“缓解焦虑和压力（relieve anxiety and strain）”，直接对应选项 F（处理压力）。
"...help clients keep the mind active so they're not so forgetful."
听到 "mind" 容易联想到心理学，但落实到 "not so forgetful" 就锁定了记忆（Memory）。
录音目的是“保持大脑活跃（keep the mind active）”以防“健忘（forgetful）”，对应记忆刺激活动（Memory stimulation）。
